entry.title: My First GitHub Project: From a Local Folder to GitHub Using Git and SSH
entry.summary:
Creating SSH key
At first I confirmed that my Github username and email were associated with Git. The commands: github config --global user.name
Generate SSH key
To generate the SSH key I ran: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "my email" The SSH key is saved to specific file location such as drive C on the laptop. The command: cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub Profile-Settings-Access-SSH and GPG key- New SSH key Add Title, Key type(Authentication key) and Paste the entire SSH key, Click Add SSH key. On Git Bash ran: ssh -T git@github.com The correct output should be that I have been successfully authenticated with my GitHub account cd Desktop - navigate to desktop mkdir 'Kenyan Health Records Analysis'- create this folder on desktop cd Kenyan Health Records Analysis- navigate into this folder touch README.md- create a README file mkdir data- create this folder within the Kenyan Health Records Analysis folder Copy the csv file into the data folder. nano README.md - open the README file so as to edit it directly in GitBash. save and exit the file. git init- initialize a Git repo. git status- shows the current status of the files git add .- stage all files/ changes for the next commit git commit -m "First commit on health records" - commits all files created to the repo. Create a new repo on Github page and copy the SSH link. git remote add origin "ssh link of the new repo on the GitHub page" git push -u origin main - pushes all files into the repo GitHub Link:https://github.com/Thuita24/Kenyan-Health-Records.git

entry.title: How TecDoc Actually Works: A Developer's Guide to Automotive Parts Fitment Data
entry.summary: If you've ever tried to build "does this part fit my car" search for an "Does part X fit a 2018 Toyota Corolla?" is not a well-formed question. engine variant TecDoc — maintained by TecAlliance, an industry consortium of OEMs and Two linked structures: Vehicle catalog — a 4-level hierarchy: Make → Model → Type → Engine Each level gets its own TecDoc ID. The "Type" level is where it gets Parts catalog — organized by Generic Article Group (GAG), a Fitment records are the join table: (GAG, Type ID) → compatible. Separately, TecDoc stores cross-reference records: IAM part number → . When an aftermarket brand submits a part, they attach The gotcha: this only works if the brand actually submitted the Don't key your fitment queries on make/model/year alone — resolve down to Type ID (engine variant) or your compatibility data will be wrong for split-engine model years. Quarterly update cycle means TecDoc data is never more than ~3 months stale by design. Fine for structural parts, not fine for fast-moving categories (filters, plugs) without your own sync discipline. Direct TecDoc licensing is a real commercial process (volume commitments, TecAlliance integration) — most teams building product pages work with a data provider instead, one that combines TecDoc with other sources and ships pre-processed, query-ready output. I wrote a longer breakdown of the full data model (including how AI TecDoc Explained — I PartWiz, where we deal with catalog Curious what other devs have run into building fitment search — anyone dealing with ACES/PIES on the US side instead of TecDoc, would be interested to compare notes.
